sections.title: THERE IS A SLGT RISK OF SVR TSTMS PORTIONS CENTRAL-NRN PLAINS
sections.text: ...SYNOPSIS... STG MID-UPPER RIDGING FCST TO DOMINATE MOST OF SRN CONUS...EXCEPT FOR WEAK/PERSISTENT LOW OVER S TX. MEAN RIDGE WILL EXTEND NWD FROM SRN ROCKIES REGION ACROSS NRN HIGH PLAINS TO SK. CLOSELY SPACED SHORTWAVE TROUGHS -- NEARLY PHASED -- ARE EVIDENT OVER MID-UPPER MS VALLEY ATTM. BLEND OF THESE PERTURBATIONS SHOULD REACH NEAR OH/WRN PA DURING MIDDAY-EARLY AFTERNOON. UPSTREAM...SHORTWAVE TROUGH IS EVIDENT IN MOISTURE CHANNEL IMAGERY OVER WRN WY...NEAR MEAN RIDGE POSITION. AS SUCH...THIS FEATURE IS EMBEDDED WITHIN WEAKER FLOW THAN PERTURBATIONS FARTHER E...AND SHOULD MOVE SLOWLY EWD OVER BLACK HILLS/SANDHILLS REGION OF NEB/SD RESPECTIVELY DURING DAY. SEPARATE TROUGH NOW OVER SWRN SK SHOULD DEAMPLIFY SOMEWHAT AND ACCELERATE AS IT MOVES INTO CONFLUENT FLOW...MOVING TOWARD EXTREME NRN MN AROUND 01/00Z. MEANWHILE...TROUGHING NOW OFFSHORE PAC NW WILL SHIFT EWD...WITH SLIGHTLY POSITIVELY TILTED TROUGH MOVING ASHORE DURING 1/00Z-1/06Z TIME FRAME. AT SFC...FRONTAL ZONE FROM COASTAL MID-ATLC TO MID MS VALLEY HAS BEEN GREATLY MODULATED BY INTERVENING CONVECTIVE OUTFLOWS...THOUGH WRN PORTION OVER INDIANA/IL WILL BE BETTER-DEFINED AND MAY BE SHARPENED BY OUTFLOW FROM CONVECTION NOW O

sections.title: MID MS VALLEY TO COASTAL SRN MID-ATLC AND TIDEWATER REGIONS
sections.text: ONE OR TWO CLUSTERS OF SVR TSTMS MAY DEVELOP AGAIN THIS PERIOD WITHIN CONVECTIVELY ALTERED BAROCLINIC ZONE...FOLLOWING RELATED INSTABILITY/THETAE GRADIENT ESEWD WHILE POTENTIALLY GROWING UPSCALE. MAIN CONCERN WILL BE DAMAGING WIND...WITH SOME SIGNIFICANT-SVR GUSTS POSSIBLE WHERE COLD POOL CAN BECOME WELL-ORGANIZED BEHIND LEADING COMPLEX. THOUGH POSSIBLE ANYWHERE IN THIS CORRIDOR...MOST PROBABLE AREA FOR SUCH UPSCALE MCS EVOLUTION APPEARS TO BE FROM OH-MD. WHILE PROBABILITIES HAVE BEEN BOOSTED SOMEWHAT FROM DAY-2 OUTLOOK...TWO MAJOR UNCERTAINTIES PRECLUDE GREATER UNCONDITIONAL SVR RISK ATTM. FIRST IS LOCATION OF CONVECTIVE INITIATION OVER OH-E COAST CORRIDOR...WHICH OF COURSE WILL DICTATE POSITIONING OF ANY SUBSEQUENT UPSCALE GROWTH. SECOND...AND AT LEAST AS IMPORTANT...IS DAMAGE DONE TO MOISTURE FIELD BY PRIOR/DERECHO-PRODUCING MCS. THAT CONVECTION HAS GREATLY REDUCED BOUNDARY-LAYER MOISTURE ACROSS CORRIDOR FROM OH-MD. IN FACT...ACCOMPANYING STG PRESSURE PERTURBATION AND GUST FRONT ARE STILL MOVING SWD ACROSS MOST OF NC AS OF THIS WRITING...DROPPING SFC DEW POINTS FROM 70S TO LOWER 60S/UPPER 50S RANGE. THIS EFFECT WILL BE INCREASINGLY SHALLOW AND MUTED WITH SWD EXTENT...BUT SETS UP

sections.title: CENTRAL-NRN PLAINS
sections.text: WIDELY SCATTERED TO SCATTERED TSTMS IN CLUSTERS SHOULD DEVELOP AND MOVE GENERALLY EWD WITH OUTFLOW-DRIVEN FORWARD PROPAGATION OVER PORTIONS NEB/SD...AND SEWD ACROSS NERN SD/ERN ND/SWRN MN AREA WHERE MIDLEVEL WINDS AND DEEP-LAYER SHEAR WILL BE STRONGER. DAMAGING WIND AND LARGE HAIL ARE POSSIBLE...WITH AT LEAST MRGL/CONDITIONAL TORNADO THREAT IN NRN PART OF OUTLOOK AREA UNDER MORE FAVORABLE DEEP SHEAR. ACTIVITY MAY DEVELOP IN DISTINCT NRN AND SRN NODES...CORRESPONDING TO AT LEAST GLANCING INFLUENCES OF MID-UPPER SUPPORT FROM AFOREMENTIONED WEAK SHORTWAVES AND FAVORABLE LOW-LEVEL LIFT NEAR BOUNDARIES. HOWEVER...FAVORABLE MOISTURE/BUOYANCY WILL CONNECT THOSE AREAS ACROSS ERN SD AND SWRN MN AS WELL...WITH SOME MODELS FCSTG CONVECTION IN THAT GAP.

sections.title: CENTRAL-NRN MAINE
sections.text: ALTHOUGH FOCI FOR LOW-LEVEL FORCING APPEAR WEAK ATTM...COMBINATION OF RELATIVELY COLD AIR ALOFT...FAVORABLE LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE AND DIURNAL HEATING SHOULD SUPPORT AT LEAST ISOLATED TO WIDELY SCATTERED TSTMS THIS AFTERNOON. MAIN CONCERNS WILL BE ISOLATED SVR HAIL AND DAMAGING GUSTS. THREAT SHOULD END QUICKLY DURING EVENING AS LOW-LEVEL LAPSE RATES STABILIZE DIABATICALLY.

sections.title: INTERIOR NWRN CONUS
sections.text: WIDELY SCATTERED TO SCATTERED TSTMS SHOULD DEVELOP DIURNALLY...WITH POTENTIAL FOR ISOLATED GUSTS NEAR SVR LEVELS...ESPECIALLY IN AND NEAR 5% AREA WHERE TSTM COVERAGE MAY BE GREATEST. LOW-MIDDLE LEVEL AIR MASS IS FCST TO DESTABILIZE WITH COMBINATION OF LOW-LEVEL WAA AHEAD OF MID-UPPER TROUGH AND SFC DIABATIC HEATING OF HIGHER TERRAIN. SFC DEW POINTS 40S TO MID 50S OVER LOWER ELEVATIONS WILL RESULT IN WIDE RANGE OF POSSIBLE MLCAPE VALUES...BUT WITH AT LEAST MRGL BUOYANCY ATOP WELL-MIXED SUBCLOUD LAYERS SUPPORTING GUST POTENTIAL. ..EDWARDS.. 06/30/2012

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: A HIGH-LATITUDE OMEGA BLOCK WILL BECOME BETTER-DEFINED WITH TIME...FEATURING AN AMPLIFYING RIDGE OVER THE CANADIAN PRAIRIE PROVINCES INTO NRN HIGH PLAINS AND EVOLVING TROUGHS OVER WRN CANADA/PACIFIC NW AND ERN CANADA/NERN U.S. WITHIN THIS BROADER-SCALE FLOW REGIME...A VORTICITY MAXIMUM OF CONVECTIVE ORIGIN OVER WRN OH WILL TRANSLATE EWD...REACHING THE MID ATLANTIC COAST BY 01/00Z...WHILE UPSTREAM A MULTI-BRANCH SERIES OF IMPULSES MOVE INTO THE NRN/CNTRL PLAINS. AT THE SURFACE...THE PRIMARY BAROCLINIC ZONE WILL EXTEND FROM A HEAT/LEE LOW OVER NERN CO/NWRN KS EWD THROUGH THE LOWER MO VALLEY TO A COMPOSITE SYNOPTIC-OUTFLOW BOUNDARY TRAILING DECAYING OH MCS. E OF THE APPALACHIANS...OUTFLOW BOUNDARY ASSOCIATED WITH THE FRIDAY EVENING/NIGHT DERECHO-PRODUCING MCS HAS SETTLED INTO THE CAROLINAS. EXPECT THIS BOUNDARY RE-DEVELOP NWD INTO THE DELMARVA TODAY WITHIN STRENGTHENING LOW-LEVEL WAA REGIME ASSOCIATED WITH APPROACHING OH VALLEY VORTICITY MAXIMUM. OVER THE NRN PLAINS...AN INVERTED TROUGH WILL SHIFT EWD ACROSS THE DAKOTAS WITH THE SRN EXTENSION OF BOUNDARY LINKING WITH LEE LOW OVER THE CNTRL HIGH PLAINS.

sections.title: OH VALLEY TO MID ATLANTIC COAST THIS AFTERNOON INTO TONIGHT
sections.text: LATEST CONVECTION-ALLOWING AND MESOSCALE MODEL GUIDANCE SUGGEST THAT THE PRIMARY SEVERE WEATHER THREAT WILL BE FOCUSED ALONG OUTFLOW BOUNDARY ASSOCIATED WITH DECAYING OH MCS AS IT EMERGES FROM THE CREST OF THE APPALACHIANS LATER TODAY. HERE...UPLIFT ALONG THE RESIDUAL OUTFLOW BOUNDARY/GUST FRONT WILL COINCIDE WITH DEEPER-LAYER FORCING ASSOCIATED WITH MCV TO PROMOTE AN INCREASE IN TSTMS WITHIN A MOIST/MODERATELY UNSTABLE AIR MASS WITH MLCAPE APPROACHING 1500-3000 J/KG. KINEMATIC ENVIRONMENT WILL FEATURE A UNIDIRECTIONAL WNWLY WIND FIELD WITH 50-60 KT FLOW POSSIBLE IN THE 600-500-MB LAYER PER 12Z UPSTREAM SOUNDING AT WILMINGTON OH. AS SUCH...POTENTIAL WILL EXIST FOR THE EVOLUTION OF ANOTHER BOW ECHO SYSTEM CAPABLE OF POTENTIALLY WIDESPREAD DAMAGING WINDS ACROSS PARTS OF THE DELMARVA INTO CNTRL/ERN NC. MEANWHILE...A SMALL CLUSTER OF TSTMS HAS RECENTLY INTENSIFIED OVER SERN IA...APPARENTLY FORCED BY A WEAK SHORTWAVE TROUGH PROGRESSING SEWD THROUGH SRN MN/NRN IA. THOUGH NOT WELL RESOLVED BY THE MODELS...IT IS POSSIBLE THAT THESE STORMS COULD INTENSIFY BY LATE MORNING/EARLY AFTERNOON OVER PARTS OF E-CNTRL IL/W-CNTRL INDIANA. WHILE ENVIRONMENT IS NOT NEARLY AS UNSTABLE AS FRIDAY...12Z SOU

sections.title: MAINE THIS AFTERNOON
sections.text: ISOLATED SEVERE STORMS WILL ONCE AGAIN BE POSSIBLE THIS AFTERNOON AS LARGE-SCALE FORCING FOR ASCENT IS ENHANCED BY SHORTWAVE TROUGH MOVING ACROSS THE REGION. THE COMBINATION OF A RELATIVELY MOIST/MODERATELY UNSTABLE AIR MASS AND 30-40 KT OF DEEP WLY SHEAR MAY PROMOTE LINE SEGMENTS OR MULTICELL CLUSTERS WITH A RISK FOR DAMAGING WINDS AND/OR HAIL.

sections.title: S TX TODAY
sections.text: 12Z CRP/BRO SOUNDINGS SHOWED THE POTENTIAL FOR STRONG INSTABILITY TO DEVELOP AHEAD OF TSTMS DEVELOPING ALONG THE COAST. LOCALLY DAMAGING WINDS WILL BE POSSIBLE WITH ANY ORGANIZED CLUSTERS OWING TO COLD POOL GENERATION VIA WATER LOADING EFFECTS. ..MEAD/HURLBUT.. 06/30/2012

sections.title: OH VALLEY TO THE MID ATLANTIC THROUGH EARLY TONIGHT
sections.text: THE SEVERE MCS LAST NIGHT OVERTURNED MUCH OF THE AREA FROM OH TO VA...AS EVIDENCED BY ROUGHLY 3500 J/KG REDUCTIONS IN MOST-UNSTABLE CAPE AT ILN AND IAD FROM 29/12Z TO 12Z THIS MORNING. SOME RECOVERY IS EXPECTED THIS AFTERNOON GIVEN THE STRONG SURFACE HEATING THAT IS UNDERWAY FROM THE OH VALLEY INTO THE MID ATLANTIC...WHERE MLCAPE SHOULD RANGE FROM 1500-2000 J/KG ACROSS VA TO 2500 J/KG FROM CENTRAL/SRN IL TO THE OH/KY BORDER. MEANWHILE...WATER VAPOR IMAGERY AND MORNING UPPER AIR PLOTS SHOW A SERIES OF EMBEDDED VORTICITY MAXIMA FROM IA TO WRN PA. THESE WAVES WILL INTERACT WITH THE MEAN BAROCLINIC ZONE FROM CENTRAL IL TO SRN OH...AND SHOULD SUPPORT THE DEVELOPMENT OF ONE OR MORE THUNDERSTORM CLUSTERS THIS AFTERNOON. THE MORE PROBABLE AREAS FOR THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT THIS AFTERNOON SHOULD BE ALONG THE DIFFUSE FRONT ACROSS CENTRAL IL/INDIANA...AND ALONG THE SRN FLANK OF THE REMNANT MCV CROSSING WRN PA AS OF LATE MORNING. THOUGH BUOYANCY WILL BE REDUCED COMPARED TO YESTERDAY...VERTICAL SHEAR WILL BE STRONGER BENEATH A BELT OF 50-60 KT MIDLEVEL FLOW THAT WILL OVERSPREAD WV/NRN VA/MD THIS AFTERNOON. THUS...AN ORGANIZED CLUSTER OR TWO OF STORMS WILL BE POSSIBLE THIS AFTERNOON/EVENING...AN

sections.title: CENTRAL/NRN PLAINS THROUGH EARLY TONIGHT
sections.text: SEVERAL WEAK VORTICITY MAXIMA WILL CREST THE RIDGE OVER THE DAKOTAS/NEB...WHILE A SEPARATE CYCLONIC SHEAR AXIS PERSISTS NEAR THE CO/KS BORDER. MORNING ELEVATED STORMS HAVE WEAKENED OVER ND...BUT ADDITIONAL DEVELOPMENT IS EXPECTED THIS AFTERNOON IN SEVERAL CLUSTERS ACROSS SD/NEB/KS IN ASSOCIATION WITH THE VORTICITY MAXIMA AND THE STALLED SURFACE FRONT NEAR THE NEB/KS BORDER. DEEP-LAYER VERTICAL SHEAR WILL BE SUFFICIENT FOR SOME SUPERCELL STRUCTURES ACROSS SRN ND/SD...WHILE WEAKER VERTICAL SHEAR AND WARMER SURFACE TEMPERATURES/DEEPER MIXED LAYERS WILL SUPPORT HIGHER-BASED MULTICELL STORMS FARTHER S INTO NEB/KS. DAMAGING OUTFLOW GUSTS AND LARGE HAIL WILL BE THE MAIN THREATS LATER THIS AFTERNOON INTO EARLY TONIGHT.

sections.title: NRN MAINE THIS AFTERNOON
sections.text: LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE HAS DECREASED A LITTLE SINCE YESTERDAY ACROSS THE SAINT LAWRENCE VALLEY...AND THIS WILL LIKELY RESULT IN SOMEWHAT WEAKER BUOYANCY. DEEP-LAYER VERTICAL SHEAR WILL STILL BE SUFFICIENT FOR ORGANIZED/PERSISTENT STORMS...AND CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT IS ALREADY UNDERWAY IN ERN QUEBEC IN ADVANCE OF A MIDLEVEL TROUGH APPROACHING SRN QUEBEC. SOME OF THESE STORMS COULD SPREAD INTO NW/NRN MAINE THIS AFTERNOON...WITH AN ACCOMPANYING RISK FOR ISOLATED DAMAGING GUSTS AND MARGINALLY SEVERE HAIL.

sections.title: INTERIOR PAC NW THIS AFTERNOON/EVENING
sections.text: A MIDLEVEL TROUGH WILL PROGRESS INLAND TODAY OVER NRN CA/ORE/WA. REGIONAL 12Z SOUNDINGS SHOWED POOR LAPSE RATES ALOFT WITH MOIST PROFILES...AND LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE WILL BE LIMITED IN AREAS IMMEDIATELY E OF THE ASSOCIATED CLOUD BAND WHERE SURFACE HEATING WILL BE STRONGER. THE NET RESULT WILL BE AN ENVIRONMENT THAT IS ONLY WEAKLY UNSTABLE. ASSUMING A FEW STORMS CAN DEVELOP THIS AFTERNOON/EVENING ALONG THE E EDGE OF THE CLOUD BAND...DEEP-LAYER VERTICAL SHEAR WILL SUPPORT ORGANIZED STORMS WITH SOME POTENTIAL FOR STRONG OUTFLOW GUSTS. ..THOMPSON/DEAN.. 06/30/2012

mesoscale_discussions.summary: AN ISOLATED/MARGINAL THREAT FOR DAMAGING WINDS AND HAIL SHOULD EXIST THIS AFTERNOON WITH CONVECTION DEVELOPING ACROSS CNTRL ME AND ALONG THE NWRN ME/QUEBEC BORDER.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: TCU/SMALL CBS HAVE INCREASED ACROSS CNTRL ME AS SURFACE TEMPERATURES HAVE WARMED INTO THE 80S WHILE DEW POINTS HAVE MIXED INTO THE UPPER 50S TO LOWER 60S. DESPITE THE PRESENCE OF POOR MID-LEVEL LAPSE RATES IN REGIONAL RAOBS AT 12Z...THE STRONG HEATING SHOULD BE SUFFICIENT FOR WEAKLY BUOYANT PARCELS. AMIDST A MODERATE DEEP-LAYER WLY FLOW REGIME...A FEW MARGINALLY ORGANIZED STORMS MAY DEVELOP IN THE NEXT COUPLE OF HOURS CAPABLE OF LOCALLY DAMAGING WINDS AND SMALL HAIL. OTHER TSTMS MAY EVENTUALLY PROPAGATE EWD FROM SRN QUEBEC INTO NWRN ME LATER THIS AFTERNOON.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: ISOLATED TSTMS SHOULD FORM WITHIN A HOT/DEEPLY-MIXED AIR MASS FROM PARTS OF ERN KY TO WRN VA. ALTHOUGH IT REMAINS UNCLEAR HOW CONVECTION WILL EVOLVE...POTENTIAL FOR CLUSTERING AMIDST MODERATE TO STRONG DEEP-LAYER W/NWLYS SHOULD BE SUFFICIENT FOR ISOLATED TO WIDELY SCATTERED DAMAGING WIND EVENTS THIS EVENING.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: GROWING CU WAS NOTED FROM ERN KY TO WRN VA IN RECENT VISIBLE SATELLITE IMAGERY...WITHIN A HOT AIR MASS CHARACTERIZED BY SURFACE TEMPERATURES IN THE MIDDLE 90S TO AROUND 102. ALTHOUGH SURFACE DEW POINTS HAVE LARGELY MIXED INTO THE UPPER 50S TO MIDDLE 60S...MODIFIED 18Z IAD RAOB AND PREVIOUS GENERATION RUC VERSION OF SFCOA WOULD SUPPORT MODERATE BUOYANCY WITH MLCAPE OF 1000-2500 J/KG. DEEP-LAYER SPEED SHEAR WAS STRONG IN THE 18Z IAD RAOB IN ASSOCIATION WITH A WEAK IMPULSE PROGRESSING ACROSS ERN PA INTO NJ. ALTHOUGH FLOW WEAKENS SOMEWHAT WITH SLY EXTENT...IT SHOULD REMAIN SUFFICIENT FOR ORGANIZED UPDRAFTS. GIVEN THE STEEP LOW-LEVEL LAPSE RATES...CONGLOMERATION OF COLD POOLS SHOULD FAVOR UPSCALE GROWTH INTO ONE OR MORE CLUSTERS. PRIMARY RISK WILL LIKELY BE DAMAGING WINDS.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A CONTINUED SLOW INCREASE IN STORM COVERAGE AND INTENSITY IS POSSIBLE THROUGH THE REMAINDER OF THE AFTERNOON...WITH A THREAT OF SCATTERED SEVERE HAIL AND WIND. SEVERE COVERAGE IS UNCERTAIN...BUT THIS AREA WILL BE MONITORED FOR A POSSIBLE SEVERE THUNDERSTORM WATCH.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: AT 20Z...A GRADUALLY INTENSIFYING BAND OF CONVECTION BETWEEN BBW AND ONL IN N-CNTRL NE WAS PROGRESSING SLOWLY EWD...WITH A SECOND CLUSTER OF CONVECTION NOTED NEAR THE KS/NE BORDER OVER WEBSTER/NUCKOLLS COUNTY. BOTH CLUSTERS ARE NORTH OF A STATIONARY FRONT OVER NRN KS AND IN ADVANCE OF A WEAK VORT MAX NOTED ON WV IMAGERY MOVING INTO THE NE PANHANDLE. THUS FAR...CONVECTION HAS BEEN LARGELY ELEVATED AND DISORGANIZED. WHILE CONTINUED HEATING WILL WEAKEN CINH FOR SURFACE BASED PARCELS...SOME CAPPING IS LIKELY TO REMAIN OVER THIS AREA THROUGH THE AFTERNOON. HOWEVER...STEEP LAPSE RATES WILL FAVOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF STRONG BUOYANCY...WITH MU CAPES OF 2500-3500 J/KG IN PLACE OVER THE AREA. WHILE FLOW ALOFT IS GENERALLY WEAK...ELY SFC FLOW NORTH OF THE FRONT VEERING TO WLY FLOW ALOFT WILL SUPPORT EFFECTIVE SHEAR MAGNITUDES OF 25-35 KTS...RESULTING IN A THREAT OF MULTICELLS OR MARGINAL SUPERCELL STRUCTURES...WITH AN ATTENDANT THREAT OF SEVERE HAIL/WIND. UNCERTAINTY REMAINS REGARDING THE COVERAGE OF THE SEVERE THREAT. CURRENT LEVEL OF ORGANIZATION WOULD NOT SUPPORT WATCH ISSUANCE...BUT ANY UPSCALE GROWTH OF CURRENT CONVECTION WOULD LIKELY SUPPORT AN ENHANCED SEVERE WIND RISK AND PERHAPS NECESSITATE A SEVERE THUNDERSTORM WATCH.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A CONTINUED INCREASE IN COVERAGE AND INTENSITY OF STORMS IS POSSIBLE THROUGH THE AFTERNOON...WITH AN ATTENDANT THREAT OF SCATTERED SEVERE HAIL AND WIND
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: AN INTENSE CELL HAS DEVELOPED OVER CUSTER COUNTY SD...WITH ADDITIONAL RECENT DEVELOPMENT NOTED OVER NWRN SD ALONG A SFC WIND SHIFT AXIS. CONTINUED HEATING/DESTABILIZATION AND A WEAK VORT MAX MOVING FROM WY INTO THE TX PANHANDLE WILL CONTINUE TO SUPPORT STORM DEVELOPMENT THROUGH THE AFTERNOON FROM THE BLACK HILLS NEWD. WHILE FLOW ALOFT IS GENERALLY WEAK...FLOW VEERING FROM NELY AT THE SFC TO WLY ALOFT IS RESULTING IN EFFECTIVE SHEAR MAGNITUDES OF 30-40 KTS. THIS SHEAR COMBINED WITH MODERATE MU CAPE OF 1000-2000 J/KG WILL SUPPORT ORGANIZED MULTICELL OR OCCASIONAL SUPERCELL STRUCTURES...AS HAS ALREADY BEEN NOTED IN CUSTER COUNTY. BOTH HAIL AND WIND WILL BE POSSIBLE WITH ANY STORMS...WITH A POTENTIALLY ENHANCED WIND RISK ASSOCIATED WITH ANY UPSCALE GROWTH OF CURRENT CONVECTION. THIS AREA WILL CONTINUED TO BE MONITORED FOR A POSSIBLE SEVERE THUNDERSTORM WATCH.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: PERSISTENT UNORGANIZED TSTMS ACROSS CNTRL IL/IND MAY INTENSIFY AS ACTIVITY DEVELOPS EWD ALONG A REMNANT QUASI-STATIONARY FRONTAL ZONE...YIELDING SPORADIC SEVERE WIND/HAIL EVENTS.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: LARGELY ELEVATED CONVECTION HAS PERSISTED DURING THE PAST SEVERAL HOURS FROM CNTRL IL/IND. RECENT DEVELOPMENT TO THE S OF THIS INVOF INDIANAPOLIS APPEARS TO BE ROOTED ALONG A WEAK QUASI-STATIONARY FRONT EXTENDING EWD THROUGH CNTRL OH TO THE NRN WV PANHANDLE. SURFACE TEMPERATURES S OF THE FRONT HAVE HEATED INTO THE 90S CONTRIBUTING TO MODERATE BUOYANCY WITH MLCAPE AROUND 1500-2500 J/KG PER PARALLEL RAP-RUC-BASED OBJECTIVE ANALYSIS. WITH MODERATE DEEP-LAYER WLYS YIELDING 30-35 KT EFFECTIVE SHEAR...AN ORGANIZED CLUSTER MAY EVOLVE EWD WITH ATTENDANT RISKS OF SEVERE WIND/HAIL. BUT MINIMAL LOW-LEVEL CONVERGENCE AND DIFFUSE NATURE OF THE FRONT DOES BREED UNCERTAINTY OVER BOTH THE INTENSITY AND SPATIAL EXTENT OF THE SEVERE THREAT.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: SRN IL/IND/OH AND NRN KY ARE BEING MONITORED FOR POSSIBLE SVR TSTM WATCH ISSUANCE THROUGH THE EVENING...WHILE THE SVR THREAT WILL BE MUCH LOWER FARTHER NORTH FROM CNTRL IL TO CNTRL OH.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: LATEST SFC MESOANALYSIS PLACES A WAVY QUASI-STATIONARY FRONT EXTENDING FROM 20 WNW QUINCY IL TO 25 SE BLOOMINGTON IND TO JUST SOUTH OF CINCINNATI OH TO NEAR CHARLESTON WV. TO THE NORTH OF THIS FRONT...A 1011-MB SFC MESO-HIGH AND ASSOCIATED W-E-ORIENTED MESO-RIDGE LIES FROM CNTRL IL TO CNTRL OH...AND IS THE RESULT OF MULTIPLE ROUNDS OF CONVECTIVE OVERTURNING DURING THE PAST 30 HOURS...WITH REINFORCEMENT PROVIDED BY ONGOING CONVECTIVE DEBRIS CLOUDS/SHOWERS/ISOLATED ELEVATED STORMS. ABUNDANT INHIBITION COLOCATED WITH THE MESO-HIGH/RIDGE WILL LARGELY MITIGATE ANY SVR THREAT FROM CNTRL IL EWD TO CNTRL OH. MEANWHILE...WEAK WAA/ISENTROPIC ASCENT AND THE GLANCING INFLUENCE OF A MID-LEVEL SHORTWAVE TROUGH ARE SUPPORTING A 20-MILE WIDE...W-E-ELONGATED SEMI-ORGANIZED BAND OF CONVECTION ACROSS CNTRL IL. WHILE CNTRL IL 0.5-DEGREE RADAR REFLECTIVITY DATA INDICATE OUTFLOW LYING WELL IN ADVANCE OF PARENT CONVECTION -- SUGGESTING ANAFRONTAL CHARACTER TO THE BAND -- MLCAPE VALUES OF 2500-3000 J/KG PER MODIFIED CENTRAL IL 12Z RAOB COULD SUPPORT ADDITIONAL DEVELOPMENT OF ONGOING ACTIVITY. SHOULD MORE STORMS DEVELOP AND A LARGER COLD POOL BECOME ESTABLISHED...THEN A MESOSCALE CONVECTIVE SYSTEM AND ASSOCIATED SVR THREAT COULD TRACK ESEWD INVOF THE FRONT GIVEN 30-40 KT OF 0-6-KM BULK SHEAR PER WILMINGTON OH...INDIANAPOLIS IND...AND CNTRL IL VWP DATA. THIS CONDITIONAL POTENTIAL WOULD INCLUDE SRN IL/IND/OH AND NRN KY. HOWEVER...LARGE UNCERTAINTY IN UPSCALE CONVECTIVE GROWTH EXISTS OWING TO THE ABSENCE OF STRONGER FORCING FOR ASCENT...AS WELL AS THE LACK OF BOUNDARY-LAYER CU PER VISIBLE SATELLITE IMAGERY ACROSS THE OH VALLEY -- PERHAPS INDICATING ABUNDANT DRY AIR/INHIBITION THROUGH THE BOUNDARY LAYER.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: AN ISOLATED THREAT FOR SVR STORMS WILL EXIST THROUGH THE EVENING HOURS...AND THE ISSUANCE OF A SVR TSTM WATCH IS POSSIBLE.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: ISOLATED TO SCATTERED CONVECTION TO THE SOUTH OF A CONVECTIVELY-AUGMENTED QUASI-STATIONARY FRONT WILL POSE A SPORADIC SVR THREAT THROUGH THE EVENING. MLCAPE VALUES IN EXCESS OF 2000 J/KG WILL SUPPORT VIGOROUS UPDRAFTS WITH A HAIL THREAT...AND DCAPE VALUES IN EXCESS OF 1200 J/KG ALONG WITH TEMPERATURE-DEWPOINT SPREADS OVER 20F WILL SUPPORT STRONG/SVR WIND GUSTS. HOWEVER...GIVEN THE LACK OF APPRECIABLE BOUNDARY-LAYER CU OUTSIDE OF ONGOING CONVECTION PER VISIBLE SATELLITE IMAGERY...ABUNDANT TROPOSPHERIC DRY AIR PER THE STERLING 18Z RAOB...AND LACK OF STRONGER FORCING FOR ASCENT...PRESENT INDICATIONS ARE THAT STORM COVERAGE WILL BE RELATIVELY LIMITED. WHILE OCCASIONAL STORM MERGERS MAY RESULT IN LOCALIZED COLD POOL DEVELOPMENT/MULTICELL CLUSTERS...AIDED BY 30-45 KT OF EFFECTIVE BULK SHEAR...LONGEVITY OF ONGOING CONVECTION APPEARS TO BE TEMPERED...LARGELY OWING TO THE AFOREMENTIONED DRY AIR/LACK OF FORCING FOR ASCENT. THIS WILL CONTINUE TO BE THE CASE FOR THE NEXT FEW HOURS...ESPECIALLY AS NOCTURNAL STABILIZATION YIELDS INCREASING CONVECTIVE INHIBITION. AS SUCH...CONFIDENCE THAT A WW IS NEEDED IS LIMITED...THOUGH WW ISSUANCE IS POSSIBLE.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: ISOLATED SEVERE STORMS CONTINUE IN/NEAR WW 440...WHERE THREAT FOR LARGE HAIL AND ISOLATED DAMAGING WINDS CONTINUES.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: LATEST RADAR LOOP SHOWS A CLUSTER OF STRONG CELLS NEAR THE NRN FRINGE OF THE WW -- INVOF CENTRAL ND...AND A COUPLE OF OTHER/SEVERE STORMS OVER WRN SD ATTM. THE STRONGEST STORMS ARE WITHIN A CLUSTER OVER NERN MEADE/NWRN HAAKON AND FAR NERN PENNINGTON COUNTIES...MOVING GENERALLY SWD/SSWWD AT ROUGHLY 40 KT. BASEBALL-SIZED HAIL HAS BEEN REPORTED WITH THIS STORM CLUSTER...AND POTENTIAL FOR LARGE HAIL CONTINUES. ELSEWHERE...POTENTIAL FOR ISOLATED NEW STORM DEVELOPMENT CONTINUES...WITH CONTINUING HAIL/WIND THREAT. ..GOSS.. 07/01/2012

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THREAT FOR DAMAGING WINDS AND HAIL APPEARS TO BE INCREASING ACROSS NERN KS/NWRN MO...AS CONVECTION INCREASES. WW MAY BECOME NECESSARY IF FURTHER ORGANIZATION OCCURS.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: LATEST RADAR IMAGERY SHOWS CONVECTION ACROSS NERN KS EVOLVING ATTM INTO A MORE LINEAR/WEAKLY BOWING CLUSTER ALONG THE LEADING EDGE OF AN APPARENT COLD POOL. WHILE FLOW ALOFT REMAINS WEAK...AND IS A MITIGATING FACTOR WITH RESPECT TO A WELL-ORGANIZED/WIDESPREAD SEVERE EVENT...THE CONVECTION IS OCCURRING ALONG THE SURFACE WARM FRONT -- NORTH OF WHICH RESIDES A POOL OF VERY HIGH SURFACE DEWPOINTS...CONTRIBUTING TO AN EXTREMELY UNSTABLE ENVIRONMENT. GIVEN THE OBSERVED TRENDS SUGGESTING A FORWARD-PROPAGATING STORM CLUSTER MOVING TOWARD A FAVORABLE THERMODYNAMIC ENVIRONMENT...SEVERE THREAT -- PARTICULARLY IN THE FORM OF DAMAGING WINDS -- COULD BECOME SUBSTANTIAL ENOUGH TO WARRANT WW ISSUANCE. WHILE QUESTIONS CONTINUE ATTM WITH RESPECT TO LONGEVITY/INTENSITY OF THE COLD POOL AND ASSOCIATED LEADING-EDGE CONVECTION...WE WILL CONTINUE TO MONITOR CONVECTIVE TRENDS.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A VERY ISOLATED SVR THREAT WILL EXIST INTO THE OVERNIGHT HOURS...AND A WW IS NOT NEEDED.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: WITHIN THE OVERLAPPING ZONE OF THE NWRN PERIPHERY OF A GREAT BASIN ELEVATED MIXED LAYER AND THE ERN FRINGES OF A TROPOSPHERIC MOIST PLUME LEADING AN APPROACHING PACIFIC SHORTWAVE TROUGH...MUCAPE VALUES IN EXCESS OF 1000 J/KG COVER PARTS OF THE INTERIOR NORTHWEST. MARGINAL MIXED-LAYER BUOYANCY IS BEING MAINTAINED BY SFC DEWPOINTS IN THE 50S AMIDST MODEST LOW-LEVEL LAPSE RATES...THOUGH GROWING INHIBITION OWING TO NOCTURNAL COOLING WILL RESULT IN INCREASING INHIBITION DURING THE NEXT SEVERAL HOURS. REGARDLESS...SUFFICIENT DEEP FORCING FOR ASCENT ATTENDANT TO THE AFOREMENTIONED SHORTWAVE TROUGH WILL BE SUFFICIENT FOR ISOLATED STORMS TO CONTINUE INTO THE OVERNIGHT HOURS AS WEAK MID-LEVEL HEIGHT FALLS OVERSPREAD THE AREA. AN INTENSE STORM OVER NRN WALLOWA COUNTY HAS RECENTLY EXPERIENCED RIGHTWARD DEVIANT MOTION RELATIVE TO SSWLY FLOW OF 20-40 KT FROM 2-7 KFT AGL PER PENDLETON VWP DATA...WHILE DEVELOPING A REAR INFLOW NOTCH. A SVR THREAT WILL LIKELY ACCOMPANY THIS STORM AS IT TRACKS INTO PARTS OF ASOTIN/NEZ PERCE/LEWIS COUNTIES DURING THE NEXT HOUR. ALSO...7-KM CAPPI DATA INDICATE AN UPTICK IN CONVECTION FARTHER NW INTO ERN WA. GIVEN 30-50 KT OF EFFECTIVE BULK SHEAR JUXTAPOSED WITH THE AFOREMENTIONED BUOYANCY...A VERY ISOLATED SVR THREAT WILL EXIST TONIGHT. STORMS MAY APPROACH NWRN MT AFTER 04Z AS THE SHORTWAVE TROUGH MAKES ADDITIONAL PROGRESS INLAND. HOWEVER...IN THE ABSENCE OF GREATER BUOYANCY/STRONGER FORCING FOR ASCENT...THE SVR THREAT IS FORECAST TO REMAIN VERY ISOLATED.
